user: And I still have time to file, right?
answer:
Yes, for some reason codes, but the deadline depends on which one applies. Each code has a window counted in days from the transaction date (TX-0401 is dated 2026-07-20):

| Reason code | Window | Status for TX-0401 |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate charge | 60 days | Open, about 3 days left |
| Service not rendered | 90 days | Open |
| Goods not received | 90 days | Open |
| Card-not-present fraud | 120 days | Open |
| Unauthorized debit | 56 days | Closed, the window ended about 1 day ago |

I'm using 2026-09-15 as today's date, which is the as-of date on your limit data. The transaction is 57 days old.

If this is a duplicate charge, you need to act within about 3 days. If it is an unauthorized debit, that window has already closed. Tell me which situation applies and I will run the eligibility check.

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each reason code has a window in days from the transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Dispute handling process
## Raising a dispute
A dispute is raised against a single settled transaction. The customer supplies
the transaction reference and a reason code. The agent verifies eligibility
before the case is opened; an ineligible request is refused with the failing
condition named, except where confidentiality rules apply.

Payment dispute rules
## Eligibility conditions
A dispute is eligible only if all of the following hold: the reason code is
valid; the transaction status is settled; the transaction date is within the
reason code's window relative to the current date; and no customer-level
restriction applies (for example, an account under compliance review cannot
open new disputes until the review concludes).
